title: DNS Systems: Name Resolution
subject: DNS Architecture
description: Resolve complex resolution failures and service record gaps in an enterprise environment.
reportOverview: This module tests your ability to distinguish between network connectivity and name resolution service health.

tickets.title: Workstation: 'The Trust Relationship Failed'
tickets.summary: A user cannot log in. Ping to the DC works via IP, but the computer cannot find the Domain Controller by name during login.
artifact: Event Viewer: 'No DNS servers could be reached to locate the DC'
Red Herring: The 'Workstation' service is running on the client

triage.q: Since the IP is reachable but the service is not, which DNS record type is likely missing for AD discovery?
options: A (Address) Record
SRV (Service) Record
MX (Mail) Record
CNAME (Alias) Record

diagnosis.q: Why is the _msdcs folder empty in the DNS console?
options: The Domain Controller failed to register its SRV records
The client has a corrupt HOSTS file
The zone is configured as Secondary (Read-Only)
Active Directory is in 'Safe Mode'

fix.q: What command or action forces the DC to re-publish its service records to DNS?
options: Restart the 'Netlogon' service on the Domain Controller
Run 'ipconfig /flushdns' on all client workstations
Reinstall the DNS role on the server
Rejoin the DC to the domain

debrief.summary: Active Directory lives and dies by SRV records.
debrief.takeaway: Connectivity (Ping) is just the foundation; Service Discovery (SRV) is the application layer that allows AD to function.

tickets.title: Stale Records: 'Old' IP causing 404s
tickets.summary: The FileServer was moved to 10.0.0.50, but half the users are still being directed to the old IP 10.0.0.20.
artifact: Red Herring: The server's NIC has 'Register this connection in DNS' checked

triage.q: What happens when a single name has two 'A' records with different IP addresses in DNS?
options: DNS uses Round Robin to alternate between them
DNS always picks the first one in the list
The server crashes
The client chooses the fastest IP

diagnosis.q: Why is the old record (10.0.0.20) still present after the server changed IPs?
options: The server didn't send a delete command
Scavenging is disabled, preventing 'stale' records from being auto-deleted
The ISP is caching the old record
The TTL is set to 0

fix.q: How do you ensure stale records are cleaned up automatically in the future?
options: Manually delete the old record and enable Scavenging/Aging on the zone
Restart the DNS service every 24 hours
Delete the Forward Lookup Zone and recreate it
Change the subnet mask

debrief.takeaway: Without an automated cleanup process, DNS becomes cluttered with 'ghost' records that cause intermittent failures.
